findings.title: P2 Remove undocumented absolute limits on affine parameters
findings.body: The public contracts require finite parameters and independently justified arithmetic bounds, but impose no absolute 1e6 limit on coefficients or derived intercepts. This rejects numerically resolvable, contract-compliant checkpoints: for example, b=300000, mref=5, a=d=e=rho=0 and rawsigma=300000 produce an intercept of -1500000 with a well-scaled likelihood, yet fail here before Gaussian completion or the arithmetic-bound checks. The similar parameter_domain restriction in shape_state also adds an undocumented admission condition. Remove these arbitrary limits and let the specified representation and operation-aware checks determine whether replay is resolvable.

overall_explanation: The auditor introduces undocumented magnitude restrictions that can reject otherwise valid saved checkpoints before performing the required numerical checks. Review was limited to source inspection; no tests or numerical model runs were performed.
